issues.legal_issue: The first hearing for tendering rent arrears in a rent-control eviction proceeding is the date when the court applies its mind to the case, not merely the returnable date stated in the summons.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground of rent default.

On the returnable date, the tenant appeared and sought time to file a written statement; the matter was adjourned without the Rent Controller assessing the application costs or taking up the hearing of the case.
On the next date, the tenant filed a written statement and tendered the arrears, interest, and costs assessed by the Rent Controller.
The Rent Controller treated the returnable date as the first hearing and ordered eviction; the appellate authority held the later tender valid, but the High Court restored the eviction order.
issues.conclusion: The returnable date was not the first hearing. The tenant's tender on the later date, when the application costs were assessed, was valid; the eviction order was set aside and the application for eviction dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to section 13(2)(i) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, the tenant must tender the rent arrears, interest, and assessed application costs by the first hearing. Because the Act is beneficial legislation intended to protect tenants, “first hearing” means the date when the court applies its mind to the case, not the returnable date. The Court followed Ved Prakash v. Vishwa Mohan, which interpreted a pari materia provision, and approved Mangat Rai v. Ved Prakash, Shah Ambalal Chhotalal v. Shah Babal Das Dayabhai, and Khanderao Malkarjun Dhotre v. Anandrao Laxmanrao Mashalkar. The Court also relied on the procedural significance of preliminary examination and settlement of issues reflected in Orders 10, 14, and 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

rule.if: rent_default_eviction_proceeding and appearance_was_only_for_appearance and hearing_had_not_started and costs_not_assessed_on_return_date and tender_made_when_costs_were_assessed

predicates.rent_default_eviction_proceeding: A landlord initiated a rent-control proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant for rent default.
predicates.appearance_was_only_for_appearance: On the summons return date, the tenant appeared and sought time to file a written response, and the court adjourned the matter.
predicates.hearing_had_not_started: The court had not yet taken up the case for hearing or applied its mind to it.
predicates.costs_not_assessed_on_return_date: The court had not assessed the application costs on the summons return date.
predicates.tender_made_when_costs_were_assessed: The tenant tendered the rent arrears, interest, and costs on a later date when the court assessed those costs.

issues.definition: When a tenant facing rent-default eviction appears only for the return date, the hearing has not begun, costs remain unassessed, and the tenant tenders the required amounts when those costs are assessed, the tender is timely.
